minutes.headline: Commission to seek Town Meeting authority to set its own wetlands permit fee schedule, vote due mid-September
minutes.summary: The Conservation Commission worked through six wetlands hearings — continuing four (a boat ramp, a driveway crossing, an irrigation pond, and a Unitil substation) and approving two (a wetland-crossing home site and a driveway/rain garden) — plus a septic repair and a certificate of compliance. In other business it discussed pursuing town meeting authority to set its own fee schedule, approved small expenditures for an Eagle Scout picnic-table project and shed shingles, and took up trail maintenance and the future use of the commission's Hollis Road house.

what_happened.line: The commission plans to ask Town Meeting for authority to set its own wetlands permit fee schedule, with its own vote due by mid-September.
It approved a wetland crossing at 507 West Townsend Road with added planting and two growing seasons of monitoring, and a driveway/rain garden at 91 Round Road.
Four other hearings were continued, including a boat ramp, a driveway crossing where an abutter described existing flooding, and an irrigation pond an abutter said could drain her own pond.
The agent was directed to warn Unitil that continued non-responsiveness on its substation hearing could lead the commission to vote without them.
Small expenditures were approved for an Eagle Scout picnic-table project and shed shingles, and the future use of the commission's Hollis Road house is under discussion.

why_it_matters: A move to let the commission set its own fee schedule would change how wetlands permit costs are set for property owners doing work near wetlands, subject to a Town Meeting vote.
watch_next: Commission vote on the fee-schedule warrant article, expected by mid-September, once all commissioners are present.
Continued hearings return August 19 (boat ramp, irrigation pond, Unitil substation) and September 2 (driveway crossing).
